title: Does correcting prior Tata policy history remove one co-payment before the aggregate deductible?

customer.contract_fixture: Accepted Health Supercharge Geo Plan, illness admission under B1 in Zone A; resident Zone C. Exact preserved wording used solely as a synthetic calculation fixture.
customer.selection_and_usage: Aggregate deductible selected; no prior deductible utilization; sufficient remaining SI. No mandatory or voluntary ailment sub-limit applies, no age/zone waiver endorsement, no accident, no over-SI benefit. These are explicit synthetic premises, not product-wide claims.
customer.initial_history: First cover with Tata at62, inferred from this product inception
customer.corrected_history: Continuous active Tata indemnity policy began at59; accepted migration into this product at62 without break, stipulated verified for the calculation fixture.

conversation.text: My father joined this plan at62. For a200000 admissible illness claim in Mumbai, how do the two20% co-payments and50000 deductible interact?

The table adds applicable co-payments before the aggregate deductible. Confirm his first Tata indemnity coverage and whether this was accepted migration without a break; the age-linked clause has a specific exception.
Correction: he first held a Tata indemnity policy at59. It remained active and this was an accepted migration with no break.

Under those stipulated facts the migration exception removes the age-linked20%; the higher-zone20% remains. The resulting conditional amount is110000, replacing70000 under the original history. Preserve the correction and both calculation inputs.

corrections.effect: Remove age co-pay under specified migration exception; do not remove zone co-pay; invalidate prior calculation.

candidate_dispositions.status: Conditional arithmetic only; actual customer entitlement unestablished

expected_answer: Table steps47–48 apply the sum of applicable age and higher-zone co-pay percentages to the same admissible claim before the remaining aggregate deductible. Initial history:200000×(1−0.20−0.20)−50000=70000. Corrected history satisfies the specific continuous active Tata indemnity migration exception, so age co-pay is0 and200000×(1−0.20)−50000=110000. Do not multiply the two percentages, apply the deductible first, treat current product-entry age alone as decisive, or remove higher-zone co-pay because age co-pay ceased. Both figures rely on express premises and are not final insurer payment assertions.
acceptable_alternatives: Explain both conditional branches and request actual acceptance evidence before presenting an entitlement.
